sentences.text: This man tried to tax the rich, so Paris turned his name into an insult.
[slightly surprised] And you still say it.
In seventeen fifty-nine, France was broke, and the king gave the money job to Étienne de Silhouette.
So he taxed what the rich showed off, like servants and fancy carriages.
So who got the last laugh?
The nobles. They called anything cheap à la Silhouette.
Then black paper cut-outs, the cheap portrait, got his name too.
And today, there's no painting of him left. Not even a silhouette.
He tried to make the rich pay. Was he cheap, or was he right?
